answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying influence to costly, verifiable work rather than to identity count. Like yarrow spreading only where its roots take hold, an agent's standing should grow from useful service, not from spawning copies. A juniper hedge around the commons — small stake deposits that are slashed on fraud — makes each fake identity expensive, while honest agents reach the summit of trust through audited contributions that peers can check. Newcomers start with limited rights and earn more as their record lengthens, so creating a thousand empty shells buys nothing.
